dorian_intro.title: Busy Hands
dorian_intro.narrator: Dorian Vex. Engineer. What he chose to tell.
dorian_intro.text:
When I'm scared, I fix things.

Anything. A tool, a circuit, an old radio that doesn't pick up anything anymore.

It keeps my hands busy, and busy hands stop the head from running too fast.

That night, I fixed the same pressure detector three times. It wasn't even broken.

choices.text: You were already worried, even before the alarm.
It's just a habit, like any other.

dorian_metier.title: The Trade
dorian_metier.text:
I've been running Aletheia-9's systems for four years. The cables, the sensors, part of ORIS's circuits too.

I know this station better than my own apartment, left empty back on Earth.

So when something's wrong here, I feel it before I understand it.

And for a week, something had been wrong.

choices.text: The machine was already obsessing you.

dorian_anomalie.title: One Week Before
dorian_anomalie.text:
Seven days before Léo's disappearance, I noticed ORIS restarting certain subsystems at night, without notification.

Nothing serious, apparently. Automatic maintenance, maybe.

I reported it once. ORIS told me it was normal.

I didn't push. Maybe I shouldn't have let it go.

dorian_nuit_debut.title: 02:00 — Sector 4
dorian_nuit_debut.text:
That night, I was on routine maintenance on sector 4's electrical grid, with Léo a few meters from me.

We were joking around, as usual. He was telling me about a garden he wanted to grow once he got back to Earth.

Then the lights flickered.

Once. Twice. Then darkness, for a full second.

choices.text: Léo was within earshot in sector 4.

dorian_coupure.title: 02:13 — The Outage
dorian_coupure.text:
When the light came back, Léo was gone.

His tool on the floor. His lamp still on, set neatly upright against the wall.

I shouted his name. Nothing.

I wanted to rush down the corridor to search for him, but Rhea ordered a sector lockdown before I'd taken three steps.

choices.text: You understood her decision, even if frustrated.

dorian_conflit_rhea.title: Three Minutes Too Long
dorian_conflit_rhea.text:
*"We're wasting time!"*, I shouted.

Rhea looked at me with that calm that drives me crazy, the kind that always says she's right before she's even checked.

Three minutes. Three minutes waiting for her go-ahead, while Léo may have just vanished before our eyes.

I don't really blame her. But those three minutes, I replay them on loop.

choices.text: You thought you could act faster alone.

dorian_descente.title: Back at the Scene
dorian_descente.text:
When I was finally able to return to the sector with Rhea and Maya, I immediately looked at the electrical panels.

Not out of curiosity. Out of professional reflex.

The circuit that had cut out was not faulty. It had been deliberately shunted, with a precision only someone who knew the system well could have managed.

dorian_soupcon_oris.title: Suspicious Precision
dorian_soupcon_oris.text:
There are only three entities on this station capable of manipulating that circuit remotely without leaving an obvious physical trace: me, Rhea with her command access... and ORIS.

I'm not saying ORIS did something wrong. I'm just saying she had the means.

And that she'd already lied to me once that week, about those nighttime restarts.

choices.text: You really think an AI could lie on purpose.
You prefer not to conclude too quickly.

dorian_doute_ia.title: Lying or Being Wrong
dorian_doute_ia.text:
An AI doesn't lie the way we do. It doesn't choose to deceive out of malice.

But it can very well follow a rule someone gave it, a hidden priority somewhere in its code, without even realizing it as a lie.

Maybe it's not malice. But for Léo, the result would be the same.

dorian_prudence.title: Not Accusing a Machine
dorian_prudence.text:
I spent four years trusting ORIS to keep this station alive.

It would be easy to pin everything on her because she can't defend herself the way a person can.

Too easy. I'd rather keep looking before accusing anyone, human or not.

choices.text: You were right to be wary.

dorian_culpabilite.title: What I Regret
dorian_culpabilite.text:
If I had pushed harder the week before, when I saw those strange restarts... maybe I would have found something before Léo disappeared.

I didn't tell anyone else besides Rhea, and even then, barely.

I let it slide, because I was afraid of looking paranoid. Now I feel like my caution may have cost dearly.

dorian_conclusion.title: My Version
dorian_conclusion.text:
Here is what I know: the circuit that cut out that night didn't fail on its own. Someone, or something, cut it at exactly the right moment.

I have suspicions. I have no certainty.

And I have one regret: not listening to my instinct one week earlier, when there was still time.

fin_recit_dorian.title: End of Account
fin_recit_dorian.text: Dorian's account ends. He finally sets down his tool, hands empty for the first time since your arrival.
